about.title: National City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: National City sees a steady stream of injury collisions each year, with public records showing 296 injury crashes and 412 people hurt in the most recent reporting year alone. Corridors like Highland Avenue, E Plaza Boulevard, National City Boulevard, and I-5 carry heavy traffic through the city, and Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to see more reported crashes than other times. If you were injured in one of these collisions, sorting out fault, medical bills, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with San Diego County claims. We don't charge you anything to get matched, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Getting the right guidance early, before you speak with an insurance adjuster, can make a real difference in how your claim unfolds.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like the city or a public bus, was involved. An attorney can help make sure you don't miss a deadline you didn't know existed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can collect. Insurance adjusters know this and often push for a recorded statement early to lock in language that shifts fault onto you.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Actually Lost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case. An attorney can help make sure those losses are properly documented and valued, not just handed over to an adjuster's formula.

items.question: I was in a crash near E Plaza Boulevard, should I give the other driver's insurance company a statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can be used to reduce or deny your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say and when.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in National City?
items.answer: California's statute of limitations for most car accident injury claims is two years from the date of the crash. If a government vehicle or agency was involved, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's worth getting your claim reviewed early so you don't lose the ability to pursue it.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you were partly at fault, though your recovery is reduced by your percentage of responsibility. This is one reason it helps to have someone evaluate the evidence on your behalf rather than accepting an insurer's initial fault assessment. Preserving photos, witness information, and any available crash records soon after the incident can matter a great deal.
